newsitem.title: UK: GKN sees better 97 for auto business.
newsitem.headline: GKN sees better 97 for auto business.

text.p: GKN Plc, the British engineering giant said on Thursday it expected a better 1997 for its automotive businesses despite forecasting flat European and North American markets this year, after reporting pretax profits of 362.8 million pounds.

The results, which failed to include any provisions for the legal dispute with its U.S. franchising operation, showed profits up 13 percent, with the dividend payout at 26.5 pence per share, up 10 percent.
Chief Exceutive CK Chow said the recent strength of sterling which has hurt British exporters would have some impact on his company's overseas earnings.

"Although the recent strength of sterling will not have a significant translation impact, it will affect the translation of overseas profits. Nevertheless, we expect 1997 to be another year of progress for GKN," Chow said.
He went on to describe the 1996 performance as a record one.
"All our core businesses made good progress with particularly strong results from Chep and aerospace and special vehicles."

The year ahead would be driven by productivity gains in the auto division and emerging market growth. Chow said. Aerospace and special vehicles are seen moving ahead, despite the expected completion of major contracts later this year.

On the subject of GKN's litigation with its U.S. franchising operation, Meineke Discount Muffler Shops, the group said it had made no provision in the 1996 results because there was still no final court judgement from the presiding judge.
